items.bold: MODI GOVT RAISED GOLD CUSTOMS DUTY — days after PM appeal to stop buying gold. Gold prices jumped Rs 9,000 in one session.
items.text: News24Online (2 hours ago) confirmed: the Modi government raised gold customs duty just days after PM Modi's appeal to citizens to not buy gold for weddings for one year. Gold prices jumped Rs 9,000 in one session on the duty hike announcement. This is a two-pronged austerity approach: (1) voluntary appeal on Sunday (Modi speech), followed by (2) fiscal measure on Wednesday (customs duty hike). The gold customs duty hike is designed to reduce gold import demand — gold imports run approximately Rs 3-4 lakh crore annually, consuming significant forex reserves. Combined with the petrol/diesel hike: the government has now implemented both conservation (voluntary) and fiscal (mandatory) measures in the same week. The gold duty hike adds to the consumer price burden — gold for weddings, festivals, and investment is now more expensive simultaneously with petrol at Rs 103.54.

military.t: TRUMP: Iran Response "PIECE OF GARBAGE." Aides Considering Major Combat. Frustrated with Iranian Leadership "Division."
military.d: CBS News (17hr ago) and CNN confirmed: Trump escalated his language — calling Iran's response a "piece of garbage" after previously calling it "totally unacceptable" and "stupid." CNN sources: Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Iranian leadership, specifically perceiving "division in Iranian leadership that is preventing them from making substantial concessions on nuclear talks." Trump aides are now more seriously considering a resumption of major combat operations than at any point since the ceasefire. The Iran advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader warned Trump "should not mistake the current lack of fighting between the US and Iran as a victory." Ghalibaf: Iran "prepared for every option." The escalating language from both sides — "piece of garbage" + "prepared for every option" — signals the ceasefire is under its most severe political strain since April 8.

military.t: TRUMP-XI BEIJING SUMMIT THURSDAY — White House Low Expectations on Iran. Wang Yi: Open Hormuz "AS SOON AS POSSIBLE."
military.d: CNBC (8hr ago), Chatham House, CSIS confirmed: Trump arrives in Beijing Thursday — first China visit since 2017. White House set LOW EXPECTATIONS specifically on Iran at this summit — the administration wants to prevent Iran from overshadowing progress on trade, rare earths, Taiwan, and AI. Wang Yi (China top diplomat) has called for Hormuz to be opened "as soon as possible" in talks with Araghchi. Chatham House (Ahmed Aboudouh): China "very cautious, risk-averse" — sent subtle message of discontent to BOTH Iran (for closing Hormuz) AND the US (for the blockade). "They don't want to be involved in anything that would drag them into something that they don't consider their problem." China will want something from the US in return for applying pressure on Iran. CSIS: US focuses on economy and Iran; China seeks stability and progress on Taiwan. The deal China wants = US concessions on Taiwan or trade in exchange for Iran pressure.

military.t: IRAN Lobbying Beijing — Ambassador: Relationship "TOO STRONG for US." Advisor: Trump "Should Not Mistake Lack of Fighting as Victory."
military.d: CNN confirmed: Iran's ambassador to China, Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, posted on X on Tuesday actively lobbying Beijing not to concede to US pressure — saying the Iran-China relationship is "too strong for the US to overcome." An advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned Trump "should not mistake the current lack of fighting between the US and Iran as a victory" as he heads to Beijing. Ghalibaf: Iran "prepared for every option." CNBC analysis: "China gains a positional advantage — Beijing is Iran's largest trade partner and the top buyer of its oil." Iran is simultaneously: (1) submitting proposals via Pakistan, (2) warning Trump not to feel victorious, (3) lobbying China not to pressure it, (4) preparing for every option militarily. This is Iran's comprehensive diplomatic and military positioning before the Beijing summit.

military.t: ISRAEL SENT IRON DOME BATTERIES TO UAE — Huckabee Confirmed. New Israel-UAE-Gulf Security Architecture Taking Shape.
military.d: CBS News confirmed: Israel sent Iron Dome anti-missile batteries and personnel to operate them to the UAE to defend the country during the Iran war. US Ambassador Huckabee confirmed at an event in Tel Aviv: "I'd like to say a word of appreciation for United Arab Emirates, the first Abraham Accord member." The Israel-UAE Iron Dome deployment is a fundamental new development in Gulf security architecture — Israel is now actively defending Gulf Arab states against Iran using its proven missile defense systems. This is the Abraham Accords delivering on their strategic promise: Israel-Gulf Arab security cooperation against the Iranian threat. For the region: UAE now has Israeli missile defense operating on its soil. For Iran: its drone attacks on UAE now face Iron Dome interception. Israeli strikes on South Lebanon Monday night killed 6 people (NNA). Fighting continues in Lebanon despite ceasefire.

assessment.body:
Wednesday 6:30 PM IST. Day 75. India's war economics have entered a new phase.

THE OMC HIKE — IMPLEMENTED
Petrol: Rs 103.54/L (from Rs 94.77 — up Rs 9/L)
Diesel: Rs 90.03/L
First petrol above Rs 100 in most cities since 2022.
Under-recovery still: Rs 18/L petrol, Rs 35/L diesel at Brent $107.52.
The hike addresses part of the problem. It does not solve it.
Brent must fall to ~$85-90 for OMCs to break even at these retail prices.

THE TWO-DAY CRASH
Monday -1,312 pts (77,328 → 76,015)
Tuesday -1,456 pts (76,015 → 74,559)
Cumulative: -2,769 pts from Friday's close
Rs 20+ trillion wiped from BSE market cap in two sessions
Gold duty hike added to consumer cost burden
Rupee ATL 95.71 — weakest in Indian history

THE GOVERNMENT'S TWO-PRONGED AUSTERITY
1. VOLUNTARY: PM Modi conservation speech Sunday (petrol, gold, WFH, fertiliser)
2. FISCAL: Petrol hike Rs 9/L + Gold customs duty hike Wednesday
India has now implemented both the appeal and the enforcement — within 96 hours of each other.

WEDNESDAY PARTIAL RECOVERY
Sensex +354 early. Nifty +0.25%.
Markets giving partial credit to Trump-Xi Beijing optimism.
Asian markets mixed: Korea +1.75%, Japan +0.66%, India +0.25%, China flat.
Recovery is tentative — Brent $107.52 caps the upside.

THURSDAY — THE DECISIVE DAY
Trump-Xi Beijing (May 13-15): if Xi signals China will pressure Iran on nuclear
→ Brent falls $10-15, Nifty recovers 700-1,000 pts toward 24,100-24,400

Araghchi BRICS Delhi (Thursday-Friday): Jaishankar-Araghchi bilateral
→ India raises: Indian tanker coordination, fertiliser corridor, 280 seafarers, OMC crude imports
→ India can influence both tracks simultaneously

VERDICT: Day 75 evening confirms what the tracker has been building toward: India is now fully in the war economically. Petrol at Rs 103.54. Rupee at ATL 95.71. Sensex down 2,769 pts in two sessions. Gold more expensive. Diesel higher. OMC still bleeding. And tomorrow, India hosts the Iranian FM at BRICS while Trump meets Xi in Beijing. The decisions made in those two rooms on Thursday will determine whether India's economic pain from the West Asia War intensifies through the rest of 2026 — or begins, slowly, to ease.

featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
